patient_answer: Administered at birth, or as soon as possible before 1 year of age.
Given as a single dose of 0.05 mL (at birth) or 0.1 mL (after 1 month) intradermally on the left upper arm.
A small red papule develops at the injection site after 2 to 3 weeks, which forms a small ulcer and heals leaving a permanent scar.
This healing scar is completely normal and shows that the vaccine has taken effect.
Do not squeeze the bump or apply ointments or herbal pastes to the injection site.

doctor_answer.assessment: BCG live-attenuated vaccine for prevention of severe childhood extrapulmonary tuberculosis.
doctor_answer.investigations: Verify infant weight and absence of severe immunodeficiency (HIV/SCID).
doctor_answer.management: Administer 0.05 mL intradermally on left upper arm using tuberculin syringe. Normal reaction: papule at 2-3 weeks, ulceration, healed scar by 6-12 weeks.

staff_answer: Verify left deltoid administration. Counsel mother that formation of a small pus point and scar is normal and expected.

topic: Vaccination: Birth Dose: OPV Zero & Hepatitis B Birth Dose
patient_answer: Hepatitis B birth dose must be administered within 24 hours of birth to protect against mother-to-child transmission.
OPV 'zero dose' (2 drops orally) is given at birth before discharge from the hospital.
Both vaccines are administered free of charge at all government hospitals and maternity centers across India.
Hepatitis B is injected intramuscularly into the outer mid-thigh (anterolateral thigh), never into the buttock.
Ensure the infant's Mother and Child Protection (MCP) card is stamped and saved safely.

doctor_answer.assessment: Perinatal immunoprophylaxis for Hepatitis B virus and early mucosal priming against Poliovirus.
doctor_answer.investigations: Screen maternal HBsAg status if possible.
doctor_answer.management: Hepatitis B vaccine 0.5 mL IM in anterolateral thigh within 24 hours. OPV 2 drops orally. If mother is HBsAg positive: co-administer Hepatitis B Immunoglobulin (HBIG) within 12 hours.
references: WHO Hepatitis B Vaccines Position Paper

staff_answer: Administer within 24h of birth. Ensure IM injection is given in anterolateral thigh (vastus lateralis), never gluteal.

Severe birth asphyxia or shock

Do NOT inject into buttock

topic: Vaccination: Pentavalent Vaccine (DPT + Hep B + Hib)
patient_answer: Administered in 3 primary doses at 6 weeks, 10 weeks, and 14 weeks of age.
Injected intramuscularly into the left outer mid-thigh.
Mild fever, swelling, or irritability at the injection site is very common for 24 to 48 hours after the shot.
Paracetamol infant drops dosed by body weight can be given if the baby is uncomfortable from fever.
Apply a clean cool damp cloth gently to the thigh if there is local swelling; do not massage.

doctor_answer.assessment: Pentavalent combination vaccine against DTP, Hepatitis B, and invasive Hib disease (meningitis, pneumonia).
doctor_answer.investigations: Verify age (minimum 6 weeks) and interval (minimum 4 weeks between doses).
doctor_answer.management: 0.5 mL IM into anterolateral aspect of mid-thigh. Paracetamol 10-15 mg/kg for post-immunization fever.

staff_answer: Check age and intervals (6, 10, 14 weeks). Record batch number in MCP card. Instruct parent on Paracetamol dosage.

Immediate anaphylaxis

Do NOT skip subsequent doses due to mild expected post-vaccine fever

patient_answer: Administered orally as drops at 6 weeks, 10 weeks, and 14 weeks of age alongside Pentavalent vaccine.
Given strictly by mouth (drops), NEVER by injection.
Babies can be breastfed normally before and immediately after receiving the drops.
If the baby spits out or vomits the drops immediately, wait a few minutes and re-administer the dose once.
Wash hands thoroughly after changing diapers, as live attenuated vaccine virus is shed in stools for a few days.

doctor_answer.assessment: Live-attenuated oral vaccine against rotaviral gastroenteritis.
doctor_answer.investigations: Rule out history of bowel intussusception or severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID).

topic: Vaccination: DPT Booster Vaccines (16-24 Months & 5-6 Years)
patient_answer: DPT 1st Booster: Given at 16 to 24 months of age.
DPT 2nd Booster: Given at 5 to 6 years of age (before entering primary school).
Injected intramuscularly (mid-thigh for toddlers under 2 years; upper arm deltoid for children 5 years and older).

doctor_answer.assessment: Active booster immunization against Corynebacterium diphtheriae, Clostridium tetani, and Bordetella pertussis.
doctor_answer.investigations: Verify completion of primary 3-dose series.

topic: Vaccination: Td Vaccine (Tetanus & Adult Diphtheria - 10y, 16y & Pregnancy)
patient_answer: Adolescent Schedule: Td is given at 10 years and again at 16 years of age.
Pregnancy Schedule: Td-1 is given early in pregnancy, followed by Td-2 at least 4 weeks later. If previously vaccinated within 3 years, a single Td Booster is given.
Protects both the mother and the newborn baby from neonatal tetanus, a fatal umbilical infection.
Injected intramuscularly into the upper arm (deltoid muscle).
Mild arm soreness for 1 to 2 days is the most common side effect.

doctor_answer.assessment: Tetanus and reduced-antigen content Diphtheria toxoid (Td). Eliminates maternal and neonatal tetanus and maintains diphtheria antitoxin levels.
doctor_answer.investigations: Check obstetric history and past tetanus vaccination records.
doctor_answer.management: 0.5 mL IM into deltoid muscle. In pregnancy: Td-1 early in 1st/2nd trimester, Td-2 four weeks later (minimum 2 weeks before expected delivery). If received 2 doses in pregnancy within past 3 years: single Td Booster.
references: WHO Maternal and Neonatal Tetanus Elimination (MNTE)

topic: Vaccination: HPV Vaccine (Human Papillomavirus / Cervical Cancer Prevention)
patient_answer: Target age: Girls and boys aged 9 to 14 years receive the highest long-term protection (before exposure to HPV).
Dosage schedule for age 9 to 14 years: 2 doses given 6 months apart (Month 0 and Month 6).
If starting at age 15 to 26 years: 3 doses are required (Month 0, Month 1-2, and Month 6).
Injected intramuscularly into the upper arm deltoid muscle.
Approved vaccines: Cervavac (indigenous quadrivalent in India), Gardasil 4, and Gardasil 9.
Regular cervical cancer screening (Pap smear / HPV DNA) is still recommended starting at age 25 to 30 even after vaccination.

doctor_answer.assessment: Recombinant L1 capsid virus-like particle (VLP) vaccine targeting oncogenic HPV types (16, 18 +/- 31, 33, 45, 52, 58) and wart-causing types (6, 11).
doctor_answer.investigations: Screen age and immune status.
doctor_answer.management: Age 9-14y: 2 doses (0, 6 months). Age >=15y or immunocompromised (HIV): 3 doses (0, 1-2, 6 months). 0.5 mL IM into deltoid muscle. Observe for 15 minutes post-injection for vasovagal syncope.
references: WHO Position Paper on Human Papillomavirus Vaccines (2022 Update)
FOGSI Clinical Guidelines on HPV Vaccination

staff_answer: Observe adolescent seated for 15 minutes post-vaccination (high incidence of anxiety-related vasovagal syncope).

Pregnancy (delay vaccination until completion of pregnancy)

patient_answer: Recommended annually because influenza viruses constantly mutate each year.
Strongly recommended for high-risk groups: adults aged 65 and older, pregnant women, young children, individuals with asthma, COPD, diabetes, heart disease, and healthcare workers.
Best taken before the monsoon or winter flu season begins.
Injected intramuscularly into the upper arm (deltoid).
Cannot cause the flu; the vaccine contains completely inactivated (killed) virus particles.

doctor_answer.assessment: Inactivated quadrivalent influenza vaccine (IIV4). Reformulated biannually for Northern and Southern hemisphere strains based on WHO surveillance.
doctor_answer.investigations: Verify history of severe egg allergy (most modern vaccines safe; cell-based/recombinant alternatives available).
doctor_answer.management: 0.5 mL IM into deltoid annually. In children 6 months to 8 years receiving flu vaccine for first time: 2 doses separated by 4 weeks.

topic: Vaccination: Adult Pneumococcal Vaccines (PCV20 / PCV15 + PPSV23)
patient_answer: Strongly recommended for all adults aged 65 and older.
Recommended for adults aged 19 to 64 with high-risk conditions: asthma, COPD, diabetes, chronic heart/liver/kidney disease, smokers, or low immunity.
Standard modern regimen: A single dose of PCV20 (Prevnar 20), OR PCV15 followed by PPSV23 (Pneumovax 23) one year later.
Injected intramuscularly into the upper arm.
Provides powerful protection against hospital admissions and death from invasive pneumococcal disease.

doctor_answer.assessment: Conjugate (PCV15/PCV20) and polysaccharide (PPSV23) vaccines protecting against invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) and pneumococcal pneumonia.
doctor_answer.investigations: Review past pneumococcal immunization history and comorbid conditions.
doctor_answer.management: Adults >=65y or 19-64y with immunocompromising/chronic conditions: Option A: Single dose PCV20. Option B: PCV15 followed by PPSV23 >= 1 year later (>= 8 weeks later if immunocompromised).

patient_answer: Standard adult schedule: 3 doses given at 0, 1 month, and 6 months.
Highly recommended for healthcare workers, dialysis patients, diabetics, travelers, household contacts of Hepatitis B patients, and individuals with multiple sexual partners.
Injected intramuscularly into the deltoid muscle of the upper arm.
A blood test (Anti-HBs antibody titer) can be checked 1 to 2 months after the 3rd dose to confirm lifelong immunity (titer >= 10 mIU/mL indicates complete protection).

patient_answer: GOLDEN RULE: If a vaccine dose is delayed or missed, NEVER restart the entire series from the beginning.
Simply resume the schedule and administer the next due dose as soon as possible, maintaining the minimum recommended interval between doses.
Multiple routine vaccines can be given safely on the same day at different injection sites (e.g., right thigh and left thigh).
Children up to 5 years old can receive catch-up vaccinations under government Mission Indradhanush campaigns.
Bring your child's immunization card to the nearest clinic or pediatrician; they will create a personalized catch-up schedule.

doctor_answer.assessment: Catch-up immunization planning. Vaccine-induced immunological memory persists; lapsed intervals do not impair ultimate antibody titers.
doctor_answer.investigations: Audit complete vaccination history and calculate chronological age and minimum dosing intervals.
doctor_answer.management: Administer all eligible overdue vaccines simultaneously using separate anatomical sites and syringes. Minimum interval between primary pentavalent/PCV doses is 4 weeks. Transition children >7 years with incomplete DPT to Tdap/Td.

topic: Vaccination: Adult Tdap Vaccine & Infant Cocooning Strategy
patient_answer: Recommended during every single pregnancy between 27 and 36 weeks of gestation.
Vaccinating the mother allows her protective antibodies to cross the placenta into the baby's bloodstream, shielding the infant during their vulnerable first 2 months of life.
Cocooning strategy: All fathers, grandparents, and household caregivers should receive a Tdap booster at least 2 weeks before holding the newborn.
Injected as a single 0.5 mL dose intramuscularly into the upper arm deltoid.
Replaces one routine 10-year Td tetanus booster in adults.

doctor_answer.assessment: Tetanus toxoid, reduced diphtheria toxoid, and acellular pertussis (Tdap: Boostrix / Adacel). Maternal immunization maximizes neonatal transplacental IgG transfer.
doctor_answer.investigations: Check gestational age (optimal window: 27 to 36 weeks gestation).
doctor_answer.management: 0.5 mL IM into deltoid muscle during each pregnancy (ideally 27-36 weeks). Single adult booster for all close infant contacts (cocooning) >=2 weeks prior to infant contact.
references: ACOG Committee Opinion on Maternal Immunization with Tdap

staff_answer: Promote Tdap between 27-36 weeks of pregnancy to protect neonates against pertussis.

Encephalopathy within 7 days of previous dose
